findings.text: follow-on: the guard fires only when exactly one canonical commit resolves and it equals the base; a promotable run whose manifest commit resolves to nothing (reclaimed worktree, unknown citation) yields an empty commit list and still falls to the plain `--gate <verdict>` offer with neither --commit nor --no-commit, which promotion refuses. Pre-existing and outside the plan's done_when (which is about the base-citing case), recorded so a reader knows the fix is scoped to len==1.

follow-on: the gate log's header names its revision and tree but spells the command's population as the literal placeholder `<seven on-surface files>` rather than the file list, so the log alone cannot reconstruct what was measured; the manifest's after_suite.command does name the seven files explicitly, so the record reconciles.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit-by-commit against base f87d778c9; one commit, three files (reckon/crew/recovery.py +20/-3, tests/test_the_offered_promotion_command_promotes.py +310, a new evidence fragment +93), all inside scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: the plan's done_when (docs/plans/the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot.html:276) names a test that drives a read-only run to promotable, fills only the offered command's placeholders, runs it and asserts it promotes; tests/test_the_offered_promotion_command_promotes.py::test_the_offered_command_for_a_read_only_run_promotes_it does exactly that, and the manifest records its head run.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to make the promotion the classifier and the obligations hook offer for a read-only run one crew complete accepts; reckon/crew/recovery.py:8018 now offers --gate not-run --no-commit --outcome when a promotable run's only resolved commit equals its dispatch base.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records head 2 passed EXIT=0, the base-arm on-surface subset 1 failed 137 passed EXIT=1, and a negative control EXIT=1, with the log paths.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares recovery.py, the new test file, an evidence fragment and a figures directory; the commit touches only the first three, every one inside the declared set.

justifications.durability: test_the_offered_command_for_a_read_only_run_promotes_it fails if the classifier is reverted to the --commit <base> offer (the committed command then exits 1), and test_a_run_with_commits_beyond_its_base_still_gets_its_commit_list guards the untouched branch; both assert against a base sha read from git, not a value the test handed the code.
justifications.evidence: the new test drives the real classifier and runs the offered command through the CLI (tests/test_the_offered_promotion_command_promotes.py:255), and the base revision's offer is refused with the cited-base error in logs/negative-control.log; the wider 35-file population was not finished (manifest follow_ons), so evidence rests on the seven-file on-surface subset.
justifications.fit: the branch reuses the existing same_revision helper (reckon/crew/recovery.py:804) and the promotion module's own base_sha spelling (reckon/crew/promotion.py:342), and the added comment states the mechanism without any plan, sprint or ticket identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/recovery.py:8018 compares the resolved commits to the pointer's base and emits --gate not-run --no-commit --outcome when they are the same single commit, which is precisely what the plan's done_when asks for; the run-time re-check here confirms the read-only offer is accepted (EXIT=0).
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat f87d778c9 0b576fa05 shows exactly reckon/crew/recovery.py, tests/test_the_offered_promotion_command_promotes.py and docs/evidence/fragments/the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot/the-offered-promotion-command-promotes.html, all within the manifest's declared write paths.
